title: Jensen Huang says he would come back as Nvidia's CEO if America needs him – a technique I now intend to use at my next job interview
summary: "I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."
body: Jensen Huang says he would be honoured to return to his role as Nvidia's CEO should the company's board want him. The problem for Huang is, the board don't seem to. In a statement sent to CNN , among others, Huang lays out his now clear-as-day faults and makes a pitch for his old job back. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang says. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." President Donald Trump and a cohort of silicon valley execs have previously backed the Nvidia co-founder, even if Trump did wobble his way over to backing ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook for a day. A heap of signatures were also added to a #bringjensenback petition , supposedly including Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney. Sweeney has barely come up for air he's so wound up about Huang's resignation. title: 'I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM' says Sam Altman, weeks after seeming to say the opposite
summary: Altman claims his remarks were taken out of context, but has since elaborated on his stance.
body: Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, got in hot water late last month when he said, "From a global allocation perspective, actually it’s quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time". He has since gone on to say he wants everyone to have RAM, actually, and in a conversation with Semafor , he has elaborated on what he claims he actually means (via The Verge ). Altman says, "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM. I think everybody should buy a lot of RAM, be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer. I think this is good. I think the home tinkering is great." So why the discrepancy? Altman says his comment was "misinterpreted, but there is a true part of it". He argues that the optimal way to use memory is to share it (in this case, he seems to be referring to the use of AI in home rigs), and "have it working 100% of the time. Rather than, like, sometimes off in someone's Edge device." So I guess if we all share RAM, we get more at the end of the day. I'll wait for OpenAI to share its memory with me, and then I might do the same. Altman points out that he got in more trou…

title: TCL CSOT's new OLED panels might not only be cheaper, but also have high refresh rates and hassle-free pixel burn-in compensation
summary: They might not even need you to wait for pixel compensation cycles.
body: I've had my eye on TCL CSOT—CSOT being a TCL subsidiary responsible for OLED production—for a while now. It might just be the company that brings OLED monitor prices down thanks to its use of the inkjet-printing (IJP) process in manufacturing. TCL CSOT had already said it was moving in equipment for IJP manufacturing and expected production in the fourth quarter of 2027, but the company is now showing off some pretty impressive panels made using the process. According to Display Specifications (via TechPowerUp ), at the Display Tech-Ecosystem Conference 2026 (DTC2026), TCL CSOT showed off a 27-inch, 1440p, 500 Hz gaming monitor made using IJP tech. Apparently, the company describes this monitor as having the "world's first high-refresh-rate in-panel compensation system." You already knew what that was, right? No, me either. According to Display Specification's understanding of the announcement, it's tech that "continuously adjusts image performance in the background without requiring periodic compensation cycles while the display is powered off." body: Controller Utils - Tracking for the Steam Controller 2026 inside Steam Frame! from r/SteamFrame If you own a Steam Frame and want to use your Steam Controller at the same time (perhaps even playing 2D games on a big virtual screen), you've likely had to use the passthrough, or just really know your controller. That's because, despite Valve noting that the Infrared LED in the controller makes it trackable in the Steam Frame , it has not yet implemented said tracking. However, a modder has once again come to PC gamers' rescue. Taking to the Steam Frame subreddit , user Kalluts has shared their Controller Utils GitHub project , saying, "Valve still has not released their official tracking support for the Steam Controller, so I had to take the matters into my own hands." title: Biostar announces the first Intel Panther Lake motherboard and it's tiny, but don't get your hopes up for cramming it into a mini gaming PC
summary: A mini PC with Intel's G3 chip would rock, but alas, we're left with just four Xe3 cores instead.
body: Motherboard manufacturer Biostar has just announced the BIPTL-IHT, a mini motherboard complete with an integrated Panther Lake-H processor. It's the first desktop Panther Lake motherboard to be released in retail. As spotted by VideoCardz , the motherboard range has support for up to 128 GB of DDR-7200 MHz SO-DIMM memory and can come with the following chips: Intel Core Ultra 5 325 / 335 / 336H Intel Core Ultra 7 355 / 365/ 356H / 366H Intel Core Ultra 9 386H All of these chips come with Xe3 graphics with four Xe cores, and are lacking the punchy integrated B390 iGPU (and its 12 Xe3 cores) that some mobile Panther Lake chips have. You can still do some light gaming on these integrated graphics, but you won't be making yourself a mini gaming PC with Biostar's latest. Instead, it seems like the purpose of this motherboard is to support industrial PCs, but given Xe3 graphics support hardware-accelerated AV1 encoding and decoding, one could feasibly use the motherboard in a mini media server PC instead. So much so that the game's offering 30 free days for long-gone adventurers… or a quick-and-dirty paid skip if you're so inclined. "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat," Yoshida wrote. title: New Asus beta BIOS patches now include a fresh AMD feature to stop you thinking your PC's b0rked
summary: The new memory training counter shows your PC hasn't just hung on boot.
body: Original story, November 16, 2026: Memory training is boring stuff. Your PC will spend an age running through it when you first boot your PC, or you swap in some new RAM sticks (lucky you), or you make a change which has anything to do with memory in your BIOS. Or just because your PC decides it might fancy doing it again. But a new AGESA 1.3.0.1F beta BIOS update, first from Asus (via Uniko's Hardware ), has made this whole process a lot more exciting. Well, going from not at all exciting to something is always going to feel like a bigger deal, but I don't necessarily want to oversell it. Though when you're waiting for memory training to complete it's real nice to at least have a readout to indicate that it is progressing and your PC hasn't just hung. This is the issue with memory training on PCs in the past. It was pretty damned opaque, in that you'd start up your PC and it would do… nothing. The fans would spin up, and the lights would light, but you'd have no readout on your monitor, and the debug screen on your motherboard would just have a static figure. Mine would be stuck on '15' for an age. Obviously you could just go looking up the error code and it would inform you that…

title: The latest SteamOS update improves support on Nvidia-powered PCs: makes swapping your rig to the OS less painful
summary: And a custom rig will be better priced than the Steam Machine.
body: The preview version of SteamOS 3.10.0 has just dropped, and with it comes better support for AMD and Nvidia hardware, and it's now based on Linux kernel 7.3. For AMD graphics, the latest SteamOS update adds support for HDMI 2.1 VRR (Variable Refresh Rate), FRL(Fixed Rate Link), and ALLM (Auto Low Latency Mode). This should all contribute to a smoother gaming experience with higher bandwidth video and less input lag. As for Nvidia graphics, it has reportedly received increased stability and performance, alongside support for Mesh Shaders on Turing and newer architectures. The latest SteamOS updates also fixed rendering corruption issues in Shadow of the Tomb Raider and The Surge 2. Then, of course, SteamOS now uses the Linux 7.3 kernel (which launched last month). Those are the big updates from SteamOS 3.10.0, but there are also a handful of fixes and changes. Game Mode has had the following changes: Added support for VK_EXT_present_timing Added support for ASUS ROG Xbox Ally X20 HDR and brightness adjustment Improved frame timing when using the framerate limiter with VRR Improved screen flickering when VRR is enabled while navigating the Steam UI or leaving it idle Improved cursor…

title: Chronicles: Medieval developer declared bankruptcy on the day it announced it was in trouble, but development will continue after a $5 million reprieve from Coffee Stain
summary: A new studio overseen by "key members" of the Chronicles team will finish the historical strategy.
body: In late October, Chronicles: Medieval developer Raw Power Games announced that it was in trouble . Funding for its ambitious, historical sandbox strategy had suddenly been pulled, and as a result the studio was at "real risk of closing". But it turns out the situation was even more dire than the announcement suggested, as Raw Power Games declared bankruptcy on the same day. Despite this, development of Chronicles: Medieval will continue with at least some of its original creators involved, after Satisfactory owners Coffee Stain Group swooped in to purchase the assets and IP. In a press release , Coffee Stain said that it submitted the winning bid in Raw Power's sale process following the company's bankruptcy, paying 36.75 million Danish Krone (around $5.42 million) for Chronicles: Medieval's intellectual property. Rather than acquire the assets directly, however, Coffee Stain will transfer them directly to a "newly established company" that is owned 75% by Coffee Stain, and 25% by "a small group of key members of the game's original development team." Alongside paying full purchase price for Chronicles: Medieval's assets, Coffee Stain will also fund the continued development of th…
